Anti-Cast: Understanding Containers & AI Sandboxing with Jay Beale
events.description:
@

Has your work begun to involve container security, or are you curious about AI sandbox escapes?

Join Jay Beale, long-time Linux container and Kubernetes security instructor, for a demo-filled webcast in which you’ll learn how containers actually work under the hood and how to attack, defend, and break out of them.

Jay will also show how weaknesses in container orchestration have led to AI agent escapes — giving you more visibility into a container than you ever had into a virtual machine.

If containers are showing up in your work or your threat model, this Anti-Cast will help you get ahead of them.

Anti-Cast: Using AI as Your Personal Research Assistant with Ashley Knowles
events.description:
@

How can you use AI to learn without accidentally ingesting incorrect information?

Join Ashley Knowles, BHIS Senior Cybersecurity Consultant, as she shares the methods she has developed for using AI to research, analyze, and absorb complex topics efficiently, including how to build a master prompt or skill that matches your unique personal learning method.

In one hour, you’ll get a repeatable system for turning AI-assisted research into knowledge you can trust, plus a practical approach to fact-checking outputs before they become assumptions.

If you’ve been using AI to answer questions, but not to actually learn, this will change how you work.

events.title: Anti-Cast: Cover Your SaaS with Shane Hartman
events.description:
@

When a security incident hits your SaaS environment, where do you even start?

There are no hard drives to image, no network packets to sniff, and no physical servers to seize. When the attacker never touched a single endpoint, where and what exactly are you investigating?

Join Shane Hartman, Principal IR Consultant at TrustedSec, as he takes you down the rabbit hole of token theft, OAuth abuse, and API exposure in SaaS incident response investigations.

You’ll leave with a clearer picture of how attackers move through SaaS environments, what evidence they leave behind, and where to look when traditional IR playbooks don’t apply.

In SaaS, attackers don’t break in. They register; they sign in. If your organization runs SaaS (and you know it does), an incident is coming. This is how you investigate it.

Anti-Cast: Find Active Directory Security Risks with David Horák
events.description:
@

What if trusted Active Directory security controls don’t actually protect you the way you think they do?

Join David Horák, Microsoft MVP and founder of Horizon Secured, for a free one-hour training session exploring overlooked Active Directory risks and putting common security assumptions to the test.

You’ll learn about unexpected behavior involving Protected Users, account lockouts, and RDP credentials, plus practical ways to reduce the risks.

You can’t prepare for every security issue, but you can build an Active Directory environment that’s ready for whatever comes next.

What in the Actual Cyber?! 2026 in Review
events.description:
December 9 @ 12:00 pm – 4:00 pm EDT

 
REGISTER FOR SUMMIT

Feeling rick-rolled by 2026? So are we.

Just when we thought we had this whole cybersecurity thing figured out, 2026 said, “Hold my energy drink.”

Attackers rewrote the rules. AI kicked over the table. Half the industry panicked — the other half claimed they’d predicted it all along.

What in the Actual Cyber?! 2026 in Review is your chance to cut through the hype with four free hours of risks, rants, and rabbit trails from the Black Hills Information Security crew.

We’ll show you the attack techniques that kept working all year, how AI-assisted SOC analysts fought back, what actually mattered in the biggest cybersecurity stories of 2026, our take on the Great AI Escape(s), and the security fundamentals that refused to die. We’ll even peek over the CISO’s shoulder and talk about what’s waiting for us in 2027.

On December 9, grab your favorite beverage, pull up a chair next to the dumpster fire, and join thousands of defenders, hunters, and hackers as we make sense of the chaos before diving headfirst into whatever 2027 throws at us.
